s:
Which of the following statements regarding Kakatiyas are correct?
I. Early Kakatiya monarchs had constructed Jain temples.
II. The influence of Chalukya temple architecture could be seen in Kakatiya temples.
III. Thousand pillared temple was built in 'Trikuta style', having three shrines, each dedicated to Rudreshwara, Vasudeva and Suryadeva
x:
All the three statements are correct. The early Kakatiya rulers were followers of Jainism before gradually embracing Shaivism. As a result, several Jain temples and basadis were constructed during the early phase of Kakatiya rule. The famous Padmakshi Temple at Hanamkonda is believed to have originally been a Jain shrine before later becoming a Hindu temple. Kakatiya temple architecture evolved under the influence of the Western Chalukyas of Kalyani. Features such as intricately carved pillars, star-shaped platforms, ornate doorways and finely sculptured ceilings clearly reflect Chalukyan influence while developing into a distinct Kakatiya architectural style. The famous Thousand Pillared Temple at Hanamkonda, constructed during the reign of Rudradeva (Prataparudra I) in 1163 CE, is built in the Trikuta style. It contains three sanctums dedicated to Rudreshwara (Shiva), Vasudeva (Vishnu) and Suryadeva (Sun God). It is regarded as one of the finest examples of Kakatiya architecture.
Hence, all three statements are correct and the answer is
Option (4).

x:
Jayapa Senani, the celebrated author of Nritta Ratnavali, served as Gajasahini (Commander of the Elephant Corps) under the Kakatiya ruler Ganapatideva. Although he was a military commander, Jayapa possessed exceptional knowledge of dance and music. His Nritta Ratnavali is one of the most authoritative medieval treatises on Indian dance and describes Marga and Desi dance traditions, dance postures, mudras and performance techniques. The famous dance sculptures of the Ramappa Temple closely follow the principles laid down in this work, making it an invaluable source for the study of medieval Indian dance.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).

s: Which dynasty built the Thousand Pillar Temple?
x:
The Thousand Pillar Temple at Hanamkonda is one of the finest architectural achievements of the Kakatiya dynasty. It was constructed during the reign of Rudradeva in 1163 CE. The temple is dedicated to Rudreshwara (Shiva), Vishnu and Surya, making it a Trikuta (three-shrine) temple. It is famous for its exquisitely carved pillars, polished stone sculptures and advanced engineering techniques. The temple represents the mature stage of Kakatiya architecture, combining artistic excellence with structural innovation. It remains one of the most important historical monuments of Telangana.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).

s: A musical instrument called 'Jalakaranda' is mentioned in this inscription?
x:
The Dharmasagara Inscription of the Kakatiya period mentions a musical instrument known as "Jalakaranda." This inscription is an important source for understanding the development of music and performing arts during the Kakatiya age. The Kakatiyas were great patrons of music, dance and literature. Their inscriptions, temple sculptures and literary works such as Jayapa Senani's Nritta Ratnavali provide valuable information about the musical traditions and instruments used during the medieval period. The reference to Jalakaranda demonstrates the rich cultural and artistic life that flourished under Kakatiya patronage.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).

s: Ramappa Temple belongs to which type?
x:
The Ramappa Temple (Rudreswara Temple) at Palampet is a classic example of the Trikuta style, consisting of three shrines built on a high star-shaped platform. Constructed during the reign of Ganapatideva under the supervision of Recharla Rudra, the temple is renowned for its sandbox foundation, floating bricks and exquisite sculptures. In 2021, UNESCO declared it a World Heritage Site.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: Under whose patronage was the Thousand Pillared Temple of Hanamkonda built?

The Thousand Pillared Temple (Rudreswara Temple) at Hanamkonda was constructed in 1163 CE during the reign of Rudradeva (Prataparudra I). The temple is built in the Trikuta style, with shrines dedicated to Rudreshwara (Shiva), Vasudeva (Vishnu) and Surya. It is considered one of the finest examples of Kakatiya architecture.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: Which of the following is the city described in Vallabhamatya's Kridabhiramam?
x:
Kridabhiramam, written by Vallabhamatya, is one of the important literary sources for the history of medieval Andhra. The work gives a vivid description of Orugallu (Warangal), the capital of the Kakatiya kingdom. It describes: • Fortifications and gateways • Markets and commercial centres • Temples and public buildings • Social life, festivals and cultural activities Because of these detailed descriptions, historians use Kridabhiramam as an important source for reconstructing the urban history of the Kakatiya period.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).
